texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Q: Do you have any examples of great 1-Pagers/PRDs/product specs? I’m looking for a structure I can borrow and inspiration for what great looks like.
texts.text: Q: Do you have any examples of great 1-Pagers/PRDs/product specs? I’m looking for a structure I can borrow and inspiration for what great looks like.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It’s particularly hard to find real-life examples of great 1-Pagers and PRDs (product requirements documents), in part because honestly most of them aren’t very good, but mostly because these documents have confidential information in them and thus aren’t readily shared.
texts.text: It’s particularly hard to find real-life examples of great 1-Pagers and PRDs (product requirements documents), in part because honestly most of them aren’t very good, but mostly because these documents have confidential information in them and thus aren’t readily shared.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The good news is that if you’re at a mid-to large-size company, you have the rare gift of having access to boatloads of real-world 1-Pagers from past and current projects. Don’t squander it. Pick a few projects that were big successes, find their original 1-Pagers, and study them. Seriously, add this to your to-do list for next week. You’ll learn a lot.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: For the rest of us peons, don’t worry, I got you. Below, I’ve pulled together a handful of solid 1-Pagers, with added commentary, plus a bunch of A+ templates that I love. If you’ve come across any other examples of 1-Pagers/PRDs in the wild that you can share, leave a comment and I’ll add it to the list 👇

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: But first, what makes a great 1-Pager/PRD?
texts.text: But first, what makes a great 1-Pager/PRD?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: As you read through these 1-Pagers, look for these elements that make them effective:
texts.text: As you read through these 1-Pagers, look for these elements that make them effective:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They crystallize the problem being solved in a few strong sentences—ideally near the top of the document—to focus the brainpower of every teammate in the same direction.
texts.text: They crystallize the problem being solved in a few strong sentences—ideally near the top of the document—to focus the brainpower of every teammate in the same direction.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They super-specifically define what success looks like when the product or feature ships, at first to make sure it’s even worth doing, and later to help everyone make tradeoff decisions throughout the project.
texts.text: They super-specifically define what success looks like when the product or feature ships, at first to make sure it’s even worth doing, and later to help everyone make tradeoff decisions throughout the project.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: They give the reader (e.g. engineers, designers, managers) just enough an idea of what the project will entail—including requirements and constraints—without eliminating the opportunity for (your super-smart) teammates to come up with even better solutions.
texts.text: They give the reader (e.g. engineers, designers, managers) just enough an idea of what the project will entail—including requirements and constraints—without eliminating the opportunity for (your super-smart) teammates to come up with even better solutions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: There’s a clear (proposed) timeline by which to review, align on, build and ship the project, to keep the project moving forward (and from exploding in scope).
texts.text: There’s a clear (proposed) timeline by which to review, align on, build and ship the project, to keep the project moving forward (and from exploding in scope).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In the end, if you want this document to be used, it needs to be readable. So keep it brief (that’s why I like the term 1-Pager), clean up formatting and comments anytime it starts to get messy, and put additional context into an appendix at the end.
texts.text: In the end, if you want this document to be used, it needs to be readable. So keep it brief (that’s why I like the term 1-Pager), clean up formatting and comments anytime it starts to get messy, and put additional context into an appendix at the end.

texts.orig: Again, I love the problem-orientedness, the very clear success criteria, and the overall simplicity of this document.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To level it up further, it could have crystallized the problem more clearly, outlined the details of the spec more concretely, and generally kept the document cleaner.
